+# Benchmark replay preparation
+
+## Finding
+
+The requested evidence campaign must repeat all twelve unchanged benchmark tasks only after the repair campaign honestly completes all twelve. No evidence campaign has started, no replay is enabled, and no Slack screenshot has been captured for it.
+
+Kernel's current [replay documentation](https://www.kernel.sh/docs/browsers/replays) supports explicit session recording, separate start/stop segments, and MP4 download. The official [Python SDK wire contract](https://github.com/kernel/kernel-python-sdk/blob/main/src/kernel/resources/browsers/replays.py) uses POST `/browsers/{id}/replays`, POST `/browsers/{id}/replays/{replay_id}/stop`, and GET `/browsers/{id}/replays/{replay_id}`. Its options include a duration bound and disabling audio. These sources were checked on 2026-10-11. The documentation calls replay-view URLs sensitive; none are retained in result metadata.
+
+Neither source documents an authentication-redaction guarantee. A browser restored from an authenticated profile can display private values before its first tool call. Native autofill can precede the Vault fill boundary. Managed Auth uses a separate browser and does not pass through the ordinary fill guard; ordinary private values may also be returned to the model for later native typing. Stopping recording after a DOM inspection cannot undo already-recorded frames. A single pre-fill hook therefore does not establish safe capture.
+
+## Change
+
+`runtime/cloud_browser/kernel_replay.py` is standalone preparation, with no production import, browser hook, model tool, CLI command, or activation setting written by this change.
+
+- `ReplayPlan` is off when the protected backend's `benchmark-replays.json` is absent or disabled. An enabled manifest must be owned by the process user, private to that user, bounded in size and lifetime, and match the exact team, requester, Slack channel, thread root, browser context and provider session. Current ownership is checked against the existing authoritative browser-owner registry. A tester identity or profile alone is insufficient, so concurrent ordinary sessions cannot enter a campaign accidentally.
+- Even a valid exact match returns `capture_allowed: false`, reason `auth_exclusion_unavailable`. No manifest flag can override this. Authentication, saved-access and restored-profile sessions remain uncaptured. A future safe boundary needs a separate implementation and review before any runtime capture can start.
+- The isolated `ReplayAPI` adapter implements the documented wire contract for synthetic tests. Start is video-only at 10fps, with an explicit duration from 1 to 600 seconds. Mutations never automatically retry. An invalid or lost start response is an unknown outcome, not proof that recording did not begin; no second start should be attempted until reconciled. A failed stop is not completion. The provider duration bound limits such a recording, but is not a privacy guarantee.
+- Export streams a bounded MP4 response into a private temporary file and publishes a new immutable local artifact only after successful completion. Redirects are refused. Failed, malformed or oversized downloads leave no partial artifact. Existing artifacts and symlinks are not overwritten. Export returns only a local path, byte count and SHA-256; capability URLs, headers and raw provider error text are excluded.

+The [evidence table](../verification/2026-10-11-benchmark-evidence.md) preserves all twelve initial prompts and the required four columns. Every run ID and artifact is pending. Future Slack images must show the actual exact thread in Aside, with thread identity checked before capture. Exclude auth cards and access links before taking a screenshot; no synthetic conversation rendering or invented screenshot may substitute for Slack evidence. Quoted, reported, conditional, future, negated, stale-event and foreign-account requests are refused. Saved Vault-only accounts and invited accounts cannot use this Managed Auth path.

+# Managed Auth with persistent browser principals
+
+This is locally tested implementation, not an activation or live acceptance
+claim. It implements the authentication portion of
+[persistent personal and shared profiles](2026-10-11-persistent-browser-principals.md).
+The 34 inventoried legacy profiles are retained pending a separately reviewed
+migration. No cookies were copied, exported or deleted by this work.
+
+## Ownership and lifecycle
+
+New Managed Auth flows reference the registry's persistent principal. A personal
+principal supports multiple exact-site connections; a shared principal supports
+its one selected account. Removing the old `UNIQUE(profile_name)` constraint
+preserves every existing flow and adds nullable principal and lease metadata.
+Legacy rows retain their old lifecycle; an already selected legacy row cannot
+silently become a principal-backed flow.
+
+Each consuming task records its own credential handle alongside its workspace,
+requester, execution home and thread binding. The original flow creator's grant
+does not authorize another recipient. Current membership, execution context,
+account metadata and grant are checked on selection and again after provider
+observation before returning a browser binding. Revocation during that GET
+cannot return the removed recipient's authority.
+
+An authenticated principal connection survives ordinary task stop and task-home
+cleanup. Those operations release the task's binding; they do not delete the
+persistent profile. Explicit account removal quarantines affected principal
+state and deletes that account's connection and saved provider credential.
+Other domains' connections and the profile are preserved pending verified
+session cleanup. Quarantine is not a claim that residual cookies were erased.
+
+Ready Vault logins remain a separate credential path. With a principal registry,
+a current grantee can use the exact ready login from its owner's dedicated
+credential vault. Shared mode checks that dedicated mapping and selects the
+shared principal; it does not create an empty Managed Auth connection or copy
+saved fields. The returned result still requires website account verification.
+
+## Writer and request generations
+
+Authentication reserves the same global single-writer lease as browser
+automation. Preparation runs after the execution-home lock is released, allowing
+an existing writer to close. Reservation precedes provider mutation;
+connection acceptance binds the exact remote ID and the lease remains active
+through login. A verified terminal result or confirmed connection deletion
+releases it. Unknown creation or login outcomes remain locked and are not
+automatically repeated.
+
+A current authorized retry creates a new request/event generation on the same
+connection and profile. The explicit fresh-login path retains its owner-intent
+checks and deduplicates the same event. It does not create another profile.
+An expired/cancelled request cannot adopt a late provider success; a new owner
+retry is required after the old writer is confirmed terminal. Cancellation
+immediately after a reserved renewal releases only that lease nonce, leaving
+the prior authenticated generation intact.
+
+[Kernel profile persistence](https://www.kernel.sh/docs/browsers/profiles) is a
+saved whole-profile snapshot, not live synchronization between writers.
+[Managed Auth login](https://www.kernel.sh/docs/api-reference/managed-auth/login)
+does not guarantee a fresh TOTP challenge. Successful dispatch, saved
+authenticator metadata and reused cookies remain insufficient proof of
+autonomous TOTP submission; that acceptance requires a later live challenge.
+Recording remains disabled, and no credential values or auth URLs are added to
+evidence by this implementation.
+
+## Validation
+
+The canonical runner used the lab virtual environment and `--file-retries 0`.
+The final six-file run passed **183 tests**, including **17 principal tests**,
+85 existing Managed Auth tests, 10 reuse tests, 19 reuse-security tests, 48 fresh
+authorization tests and four saved-login routing tests.
+
+Evidence lives under
+`.local/clanker-qa/findings/persistent-browser-principals/`:

+- `auth-red.log`: original lifecycle behavior failed the three new baseline

+- `auth-race-red.log`: two revoked-caller binding cases and the shared Vault

+- `auth-renewal-cancel-red.log`: the renewal reservation remained stranded;

+- `auth-freeze-green.log`: 183 passed, zero failed, zero retries.
+

+for grant revocation, membership removal, shared dedicated Vault routing,
+unknown provider outcomes, competing writers, request expiry, cancellation and
+schema migration. Provider I/O is synthetic. Independent source review passed;
+activation, legacy adoption/cleanup, browser-site persistence and benchmark

**No documented endpoint exposes historical Managed Auth internal actions proving TOTP use.**

- **Timeline:** attempt status, reached step, timestamps, browser ID, `telemetry_captured`, and optional `replay_id`; no challenge/submission history. [Official schema](https://github.com/kernel/kernel-go-sdk/blob/v0.120.0/authconnection.go)
- **SSE:** current flow state and optional pending fields/MFA choices; no documented history cursor. Authentication success alone does not identify the method used. [Official API](https://www.kernel.sh/docs/api-reference/managed-auth/get-auth-connection-event-timeline)
- **Audit logs:** API request method/path/status/time, not internal website actions. Missing `/submit` cannot establish that TOTP was skipped. [Audit schema](https://github.com/kernel/kernel-go-sdk/blob/v0.120.0/auditlog.go)
- **Browser telemetry:** historical events exist only if previously captured. It cannot reconstruct disabled capture. [Telemetry API](https://github.com/kernel/kernel-go-sdk/blob/v0.120.0/browsertelemetry.go)

Current TOTP evidence therefore remains **unverified, not disproven**. No live changes or authentication attempts made.
